To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
depletion of TPX2 from nuclear assembly extracts prevents nuclear reformation and that TPX2 is required to recruit LAP2 to the nuclear envelope.
TPX2 is required in cell-free extracts for the formation of large, functional postmitotic nuclei.
TPX2 is required to assemble a functional nucleus in Xenopus cell-free extracts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how nuclear structure is established and how it is maintained in the face of the dramatic changes that occur during mitosis.
the mechanisms of nuclear assembly and disassembly in the cell cycle.
the mechanisms by which the nuclear envelope is reformed after cell division, and our results suggest that the TPX2-LAP2 interaction plays an important role in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TPX2 is a critical regulator of nuclear reassembly after mitosis.
TPX2 is required to assemble a normal nuclear envelope after mitosis.
TPX2 is required to assemble the nuclear envelope and nuclear pore complexes in postmitotic Xenopus egg extracts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TPX2 is required to reestablish a normal interphase nucleus following mitotic exit.
TPX2 plays important roles in nuclear reformation and that it is required for proper nuclear assembly in cell division.
TPX2 is an essential factor for postmitotic nucleus formation in cell-free extracts.

TPX2 is a key regulator of nuclear assembly and nuclear envelope formation after mitosis.
